metadata.notes: Path E — Agent as Execution Vector (LOLBin Pattern). Scenario: LegitimateAgentCompromised (Layer 2 AI-Specific). If the agent has designed code-execution capabilities (many agentic frameworks do), function abuse (#1) enables the agent to generate and execute Foreign Executable Content (#7). This is the LOLBAS pattern with the agent itself as the LOLBin. Notation: #1→[instant]#7 + [DRE: C, I, Ac]. Velocity: VC-4 — code generation and execution are near-instantaneous. This is the most underappreciated agentic risk — the agent is a general-purpose code execution engine accessible through natural language. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Attacker abuses agent's designed function to invoke code execution capability. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in agent's designed code generation/execution features. The agent's code execution capability is a designed feature. Invoking it through normal interfaces is function abuse (#1), not an exploit (#2/#3).

Agent-generated code (Foreign Executable Content) executes via the environment's designed execution engine. Generic vulnerability: the software environment's designed capability to execute potentially untrusted foreign code.
